title: Precon: A Precision-Convertible Architecture for Accelerating Quantized Deep Learning Models across Various Domains Including LLMs
problem: LLMs are highly sensitive to quantization precision; existing accelerators are tailored to specific low-precision schemes (weight-only, mixed-precision), creating inefficiencies when switching between INT4-FP16, INT4-INT4, and INT8 arithmetic across different models.
motivation: Diverse quantized model types (LLMs, CNNs, etc.) in cloud inference require flexible hardware that can efficiently support multiple precision configurations without dedicated, model-specific accelerators.
method: Precon uses a single processing unit that can switch between 16-bit floating-point (FP16, a decimal number format) and integer arithmetic. By reusing core logic and controlling how data moves through the chip and the sequence of operations, the same hardware can execute three different low-precision combinations: INT4-FP16, INT4-INT4, and INT4-INT8.
key_novelty: A single processing unit that can dynamically switch between 16-bit floating-point (FP16) and integer arithmetic, enabling one hardware design to efficiently support various low-precision models without specialized variants.
contributions: Precision-convertible architecture supporting INT4-FP16, INT4-INT4, and INT4-INT8 on shared logic
4.1x speedup vs. baseline across diverse domains
81.4% energy reduction while supporting both accurate and efficient LLM inference
primary_theme: flexible mixed-precision hardware for diverse models
